_readme: HELD-OUT gloss test set (14 cases). Same JSON format as gloss_test_set.json plus a 'source' field.
HOW THE REFERENCES WERE MADE. Every reference_gloss was derived by hand from ISL grammar
properties stated in published sources, applied to sentences that are NOT in gloss_test_set.json.
The rule-based converter (gloss.py) was NOT run on any of these sentences, and its output was not
consulted. Rules used (all stated in source [1]; the summary of [2] agrees on SOV and covers questions and fingerspelling):
SOV       verb after its object.
WH_FINAL  in questions the wh-word is sentence-final.
FUNC_DROP articles, conjunctions and linking (be) verbs are not signed; 'to' is removed.
ROOT_FORM signs use root forms: no inflection, gerunds or suffixes (plurals and tenses reduced to the root).
ME_FOR_I  'me' is used instead of 'I'. NOTE: [1] lists this among facts about sign languages IN GENERAL, not in its ISL-specific comparison table, so cases relying on it are marked medium confidence.
Three cases (ho_pub_*) start from example sentence pairs printed in source [1] (its Table 3 and section 7.1),
then apply the same source's function-word and root-form steps.
WHAT THIS SET CAN AND CANNOT SHOW.
It measures whether gloss.py reproduces the published rule descriptions on sentences it was not tuned on.
It does NOT measure ISL correctness. The references were written by the same person who maintains the rules,
from secondary sources (a course report and a system paper), not from the primary linguistic literature
and not checked by an ISL signer. Have a signer or the primary sources (see [3], [4]) review each
reference before quoting a score.
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED because the sources are silent, conflict with each other, or describe rules the
converter does not implement: negation placement, modals, tense (source [1] says tense is shown with
signs for before/then/after), the male/female prefix on family-relation signs, numerals, plural handling,
prepositions other than 'to', and all non-manual markers. Report these as known limitations.
USAGE RULE. Run this set once and report the result as it comes out. Do not tune gloss.py against it.
If you fix rules after seeing failures, say so and evaluate the fixed rules on a NEW set.
SOURCES
[1] Gupta, Sinha, Bhushan, Shettigar. 'English Text to Indian Sign Language Translator'. COEN 296B course
report, Santa Clara University (student report, not peer reviewed).
https://www.cse.scu.edu/~m1wang/projects/NLP_English2IndianSignLanuguage_18w.pdf
[2] 'Sign Language Generation System Based on Indian Sign Language Grammar', ACM Transactions on Asian and
Low-Resource Language Information Processing, doi 10.1145/3384202 (full text could not be opened when
this file was written; only its search-result summary was read).
[3] Vasishta, Woodward, DeSantis. 'An Introduction to Indian Sign Language'. All India Federation of the Deaf
(3rd ed.); cited by [1]. Not read.
[4] Zeshan, Vasishta, Sethna (2005). 'Implementation of Indian Sign Language in educational settings'.
Asia Pacific Disability Rehabilitation Journal 16(1), 16-40; cited by [1]. Not read.
